author: NorthEast News Desk
body: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun spoke by telephone with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi about the Strait of Hormuz and worsening instability in the Middle East, Seoul said Friday. Reuters reported that Iran requested the call and that both sides agreed to keep diplomatic channels open.

Cho emphasized freedom of navigation and said South Korea would support international efforts to maintain maritime security. Araqchi presented Iran’s position on the regional conflict. The discussion comes as disruption around the strait has pressured shipping and energy markets far beyond the Gulf.

South Korea is reviewing whether it should contribute personnel to the region and recently sent an inspection team, but officials said no final deployment decision has been made. Iran has warned Seoul against joining military activity that Tehran views as aligned with the United States.

The exchange is developing because Seoul must balance the security of shipping routes with the risk of deeper involvement in the conflict. South Korea depends heavily on imported energy, giving safe passage through Hormuz direct economic importance. Continued contact with Tehran may help clarify intentions while the government assesses its options.
dek: The foreign ministers agreed to keep communication open while South Korea reviews possible support for maritime security in the Gulf.
headline: South Korea and Iran discuss Hormuz security as Seoul weighs role
